answer: Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 11% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. Policies are written in thread, settled in comet, and oasis lists every payout. A farm thus faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. That bill is paid per identity, so 172 aliases cost 270 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
